subject: Microbiology
subtopic: Visceral leishmaniasis: Leishmania, sandfly transmission, macrophage infection, kala-azar, diagnosis and treatment
concept: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is a systemic protozoal infection caused by Leishmania parasites transmitted by infected female phlebotomine sandflies.

content.definition: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is a systemic protozoal infection caused by Leishmania parasites transmitted by infected female phlebotomine sandflies.
content.explanation: Leishmania amastigotes reside within macrophages. Visceral disease involves the reticuloendothelial system, especially spleen, liver and bone marrow, leading to prolonged fever, weight loss and cytopenias.
content.mechanism: Leishmania amastigotes reside within macrophages. Visceral disease involves the reticuloendothelial system, especially spleen, liver and bone marrow, leading to prolonged fever, weight loss and cytopenias.
content.structure: Clinically important organism-specific structural and biologic features are summarized in the explanation and terminology fields.
content.function: The pathogen's biologic properties determine transmission, tissue tropism, clinical manifestations and diagnostic strategy.
causes: Animal or human reservoirs depending on endemic transmission cycle
Rare alternative transmission routes can occur in specific settings
effects: Anemia and other cytopenias; severe untreated disease can be fatal
content.clinical_relevance: This is an official Hematology microbiology syllabus organism/disease. Leishmania and Visceral Leishmaniasis should be interpreted using current diagnostic and treatment guidance.
content.diagnosis: Diagnosis may use parasite detection in tissue, antigen/antibody-based tests depending on region and clinical context, with confirmation strategies varying by endemic setting.
content.treatment: Treatment depends on geographic region, species, immune status and resistance patterns; liposomal amphotericin B is an important modern treatment in many settings, with other regimens selected according to local guidance.
